turns.text: (laughs) Well, I'm not sure about the secret part, but I do want to clarify that classical conditioning, as described by Ivan Pavlov, is a universal principle that applies to all living beings, not just the uninitiated or non-British people. The idea is that any organism, regardless of cultural background, can learn to associate a neutral stimulus with an unconditioned stimulus to elicit an unconditioned response. It's a pretty fundamental concept in psychology, so I'm not aware of any evidence that would suggest otherwise.
